prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a multi-tier indoor seating layout extending from a foreground wooden table (0.3–0.8 m away, bright grey) to an adjacent round black table (1.0–1.8 m, mid-grey) and a third background table (2.0–3.5 m, dark grey to black). In the foreground within arm's reach (~0.3–0.6 m), the camera wearer's smartphone at the bottom center, a handheld menu and cap on the lower right, a standing menu sign in the center, and a grey-shirted person with a maroon bag seated immediately to the left (~0.4–0.8 m away, facing right toward the table and not looking at the camera wearer) are clearly separated in depth from a navy-jacketed person (~1.2–1.6 m away, seated behind the left person and facing right) and a black-shirted person (~1.2–1.6 m to the right, facing left). Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer's view shifts slightly upward and left in frame 4 before the grey-shirted person leans forward and enters extreme close range (<0.3 m, bright white) on the lower left in frame 5, with their head-mounted action camera protruding directly in front of the lens and occluding the left side of the table and the navy-jacketed person's torso. The depth map makes the continuous 3D distance gradient between the overlapping foreground and mid-ground tabletops and the sudden close-proximity intrusion in frame 5 much easier to gauge than in RGB alone. However, the map is unreliable on distant background patrons (>2.5 m), which merge into uniform black, and on thin edges like the smartphone top and menu borders, which slightly bleed into the table surface's depth plane.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map partitions the scene into discrete foreground and mid-ground people and tabletop objects, identifying the grey-shirted person on the lower left (~0.4–0.8 m away, within arm's reach) and the navy-jacketed person seated ~0.6 m behind them (~1.2–1.6 m from the camera wearer), both facing right, alongside individuals across the right side of the round tables (~1.2–3.0 m away, facing left or inward). It isolates the camera wearer's smartphone at the bottom edge (~0.3 m away, within the wearer's reach) and tracks the standing menu sign on the center table (~0.7 m) and the handheld menu held on the right (~0.5 m, within reach of both the camera wearer and the right-side person), which partially occlude the black cap and tabletops behind them. Across the 5 frames, the left foreground person's mask expands rightward and upward as their head and shoulders enter the frame in frame 4 and lean within ~0.2–0.3 m in frame 5, increasingly occluding the navy-jacketed person and the central table. Compared to RGB, the segmentation map clearly delineates the boundary between the overlapping left-side patrons and highlights small, partially cropped background figures at the top edge (~2.5–3.5 m away). However, the map is unreliable in class labeling and temporal consistency: it misclassifies the central standing menu sign and right handheld menu as a 'laptop', 'cell phone', or 'book' before dropping their masks completely in frames 4–5, misses the foreground maroon bag and black cap entirely, and fragments the right-side people into inconsistent partial masks.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, isolating hand positions and a single mid-ground upper-body skeleton while omitting all scene furniture and objects. In frame 1, it detects only two magenta hand skeletons (~0.5–1.2 m away, separated by ~0.5 m laterally) belonging to the grey-shirted person's gesturing left hand on the lower left and the navy-jacketed person's clasped hands above it; in frames 2–5, it adds a magenta hand skeleton at the bottom right (~0.4–0.5 m, within the camera wearer's and right neighbor's arm's reach) gripping the handheld menu. From frame 2 onward, a yellow upper-body skeleton appears on the right (~1.2–1.6 m away) for the black-shirted person seated at the adjacent table, showing their torso angled to the left toward the center of the room and their head facing left rather than looking at the camera wearer, while their lower body is occluded below the frame and behind the foreground table. Across frames 2 to 5, as the camera view shifts and the left foreground person leans in, this right-side yellow skeleton shifts upward and rightward toward the frame edge, and in frame 4 the navy-jacketed person's torso and raised arms (~1.2–1.5 m away, facing right) briefly appear as a second yellow skeleton. The pose map makes finger articulation and torso orientation for detected subjects explicit against clutter, which is harder to isolate in RGB, but it is highly unreliable overall: it completely misses the closest person on the left in frames 2–5 (even at <0.3 m in frame 5), fails to detect the camera wearer's hands holding the bottom-center phone, and hallucinates upside-down torso connections and misplaced facial keypoints near the bottom-right hand in frames 2 and 3.
